question.text: The five primary Greek risk measures are:

answer.text: Delta, Gamma, Theta, Vega, and Rho
Alpha, Beta, Sigma, Mu, and Lambda
Delta, Sigma, Pi, Tau, and Phi
Delta, Gamma, Theta, Vega, and Sigma

explanation.text: The Logic: The five primary Greeks are Delta (sensitivity of premium to the underlying), Gamma (sensitivity of delta to the underlying), Theta (time decay), Vega (sensitivity to volatility) and Rho (sensitivity to interest rates). The Trap: Sigma is the symbol used for volatility, not one of the five Greeks; Alpha and Beta belong to portfolio theory, not option risk measures. Note: Definitions of the five primary Greeks (Delta, Gamma, Theta, Vega and Rho) are supported by pages 72-75 of the NISM Series-I workbook.
